record.final_answer:
Yes — it fails today, not eventually. Per the Corvane 2.3 multipart rules (parts 8–512 MiB except the last, at most 5000 parts per upload), 8 MiB pieces cap a single upload at about 39 GiB. A 60 GB tarball needs 7,153–7,680 parts depending on GB vs GiB, so it's already well over the 5,000-part limit. Also note 8 MiB is the gateway's *minimum* part size, so shrinking isn't an option — you have to go larger.

Changed `scripts/upload.sh:5-9`: `CHUNK_MB=8` → `32`, with a comment recording the 8–512 MiB / 5000-part rules so nobody lowers it again.

Why 32 MiB: 60 GiB becomes 1,920 parts, and the same setting carries the job to 156 GiB — roughly 2.5x today's size — before it needs another look. 16 MiB (3,840 parts, 78 GiB ceiling) would work now but leaves little room for growth; 64 MiB works too if you'd rather not revisit this for years, at the cost of coarser retry granularity on a bad night.

Verified: `sh -n` passes, and the part-count math above is computed, not estimated. What I couldn't do is exercise a real upload — `corvane-cli` isn't installed on this machine, and the limits come from the saved gateway docs rather than a live probe, so if the gateway has been upgraded since 2.3 it's worth re-checking whether the 5,000-part cap still holds.
